meta: Contact Oakley 24/7 Plumbing: call (888) 910-8644 any hour for a plumber in Oakley, CA. See what to have ready and what happens after you call.
lead: The fastest way to reach a plumber in Oakley, CA is the phone line, which is answered 24/7 for emergencies and for booking planned work.
intro: There is no online form on this site. You can call at any hour or send an email, and this page explains which to choose and what to have ready.

paras: Phone (888) 910-8644 for water spreading across a floor, sewage backing up, a leaking water heater or a drain that has stopped completely. The line runs overnight, on weekends and on holidays, and the dispatcher can talk you through closing valves while a visit is arranged.
Calling also works best for planned jobs, since a conversation about a [[water-heater-installation|water heater installation]] or a slow drain is quicker than a round of messages.

For non-urgent questions, write to contact@247plumberoakleyca.com. Email is reasonable for asking about a future project, a question about this site or a request about your information, but it is not monitored the way the phone line is, so do not use it for a flooding emergency.
Repairs happen at your property, so call or email instead of arriving in person.

sections.h2: What to have ready when you call
paras: A few details let the dispatcher size up the job in a minute or two. Have them in front of you or jotted on your phone before you dial, especially if you are standing in water or in the dark.
If you can safely take a photo of the leak, the water heater label or the failed fixture, keep it handy, since it helps both with the visit and with an insurance claim.
bullets: The street address and the nearest cross street
Which fixture or room is affected
What you can see: water, sewage, a smell or no hot water
What you have already shut off, such as the main valve or a breaker
Gate codes, parking notes or a pet that will be in the house
A phone number where you can be reached during the visit

paras: A gas odor is not a plumbing call. Exit the building, dial 911, and contact PG&E at 1-800-743-5000 first. Do not flip switches or use a lighter on the way out.

For a flood, close the main water valve first and kill power to wet areas. Our [[service-area|service area]] page lists the towns we cover, and the [[plumber-brentwood-ca|Brentwood page]] covers that city's calls.

The dispatcher confirms your address, repeats back the problem and says whether a visit tonight or a same-day appointment when available fits better. On site, the plumber explains what failed and gives a clear price before work starts.
Calls to our line may be recorded for quality and training purposes, and our privacy policy explains how we handle the details you share.

cta_mid: Water, sewage or a dead water heater is reason enough to call now, whatever the hour on the clock.
cta_end: Have your address and a short description ready, and the dispatcher will take it from there.
